description: Everything used to drive Photoshop programmatically: recorded Actions and the File > Automate / File > Scripts commands, the ExtendScript DOM and Action Manager, the modern UXP runtime, Windows COM automation, and the cloud Photoshop API.

tools.name: Actions: record, play and edit
tools.description: Records a sequence of Photoshop commands into a replayable Action stored in an Action Set. Each step can be re-ordered, duplicated, disabled, re-recorded or given a modal toggle so its dialog appears on playback. Actions are the foundation of Batch, droplets and one-key production shortcuts, and are saved as .atn files for sharing.
tools.usage: Window > Actions (Alt+F9). New Set > New Action > Record; Stop and Play with the panel footer buttons. Function keys F2-F12 (optionally with Shift/Ctrl) can be assigned to an action.

parameters.name: Toggle dialog on/off
parameters.description: The second column makes a step pause and show its dialog during playback.

parameters.name: Toggle item on/off
parameters.description: The first column disables a step without deleting it.

parameters.name: Playback Options
parameters.description: Accelerated, Step by Step or Pause For N seconds - use Step by Step when debugging an action.

parameters.name: Allow Tool Recording
parameters.description: Panel menu option that records brush and other tool strokes, which are otherwise skipped.

tools.example:
1. Alt+F9, click New Set, name it "Web".
2. Click New Action "Export 1200", assign F5, press Record.
3. Image > Image Size (1200 px wide), File > Save As JPEG, Stop.
4. Press F5 on any other document to replay it.

JSX: app.doAction("Export 1200", "Web");
tools.notes: Not everything records - some tool strokes, panel-only settings and a few filters must be replaced by an Insert Menu Item step or a script.

tools.name: Action authoring: Insert Menu Item, Stop, Conditional and Path
tools.description: Four Actions panel menu commands that add steps an ordinary recording cannot capture. Insert Menu Item records a menu command that refuses to record (including File > Scripts entries) without its settings; Insert Stop pauses playback with a message and an optional Continue button; Insert Conditional branches to a different action based on a document test; Insert Path stores a path for later use.
tools.usage: Actions panel menu > Insert Menu Item... / Insert Stop... / Insert Conditional... / Insert Path.

parameters.name: Insert Conditional tests
parameters.description: Document Is Landscape/Square, Document Mode Is RGB/CMYK/Grayscale, Document Depth Is 8/16/32, Layer Is Background, Document Has Selection/Alpha Channels, Document Is Open, Document Profile Is sRGB.

parameters.name: Allow Continue
parameters.description: On an Insert Stop, lets the operator carry on rather than forcing the action to halt.

tools.example:
1. Create an action "Portrait" and an action "Landscape".
2. Create a third action, Actions menu > Insert Conditional: If Document Is Landscape, Then Play "Landscape", Else Play "Portrait".
3. Run the third action from Batch across a mixed folder.

tools.name: Batch
tools.description: Runs one action over every file in a folder, over an Adobe Bridge selection, or over imported files, with control over where the results go and how they are named. The two override checkboxes are the ones that matter: "Override Action Open Commands" and "Override Action Save As Commands" stop the recorded paths being reused for every file.
tools.usage: File > Automate > Batch...

parameters.name: Set / Action
parameters.description: Which recorded action to play.

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: Folder, Import, Opened Files or Bridge; with Include All Subfolders.

parameters.name: Override Action Open Commands
parameters.description: Use the batch's own file list instead of the file recorded in the action.

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: None, Save and Close, or Folder - with Override Action Save As Commands.

parameters.name: File Naming
parameters.description: Six token fields (document name, serial number, date, extension) plus compatibility options.

parameters.name: Errors
parameters.description: Stop For Errors or Log Errors To File - always choose the log for unattended runs.

tools.example: File > Automate > Batch: Set = Web, Action = Export 1200, Source = Folder C:\in (include subfolders), Destination = Folder C:\out, tick both Override checkboxes, File Naming = document name + "_web" + extension, Errors = Log Errors To File.

tools.name: Create Droplet
tools.description: Exports a Batch configuration as a small executable. Dragging files or folders onto the droplet launches Photoshop (if needed) and runs the action over them, which makes it the simplest way to expose a Photoshop process to non-Photoshop users or to a hot-folder workflow.
tools.usage: File > Automate > Create Droplet...

parameters.name: Save Droplet In
parameters.description: Where the .exe (Windows) or application (macOS) is written.

parameters.name: Play / Destination / File Naming / Errors
parameters.description: The same options as the Batch dialog, baked into the droplet.

tools.example:
1. File > Automate > Create Droplet, save as C:\tools\make_web_jpgs.exe.
2. Choose Set = Web, Action = Export 1200, Destination = Folder, tick Override Action Save As Commands.
3. Drag a folder of RAW files onto the droplet.
tools.notes: Droplets are platform-specific and record absolute paths; re-create the droplet if Photoshop is upgraded or the folders move.

tools.name: Image Processor
tools.description: A built-in script that converts a folder of images to JPEG, PSD and/or TIFF at once, optionally resizing to fit a bounding box, converting to sRGB and running an action on each file. Faster to set up than Batch for the common "make web and print versions of everything" job.
tools.usage: File > Scripts > Image Processor... (also available from Adobe Bridge: Tools > Photoshop > Image Processor).

parameters.name: Select the images to process
parameters.description: A folder (with subfolders) or the currently open files.

parameters.name: File Type
parameters.description: Save as JPEG (with quality and Convert Profile to sRGB), PSD (Maximize Compatibility) and/or TIFF (LZW), each with Resize to Fit W x H.

parameters.name: Preferences
parameters.description: Run Action, Copyright Info, Include ICC Profile.

tools.example: File > Scripts > Image Processor: source folder C:\shoot, tick Save as JPEG quality 10 + Resize to Fit 2048 x 2048 + Convert Profile to sRGB, tick Save as TIFF, Run Action = Web/Sharpen.

tools.name: Script Events Manager
tools.description: Binds a script or an action to a Photoshop event, so it runs automatically whenever that event fires - New Document, Open Document, Save Document, Export Document, Print Document, Start Application and others. The hook used to auto-apply house settings, log activity or post-process every opened file.
tools.usage: File > Scripts > Script Events Manager... Tick "Enable Events to Run Scripts/Actions", pick a Photoshop Event, choose a Script or an Action, click Add.

parameters.name: Photoshop Event
parameters.description: Start Application, New Document, Open Document, Save Document, Close Document, Export Document, Print Document, Stop Application.

parameters.name: Script
parameters.description: One of the bundled scripts or Browse for your own .jsx.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: Any set/action pair instead of a script.

tools.example:
1. File > Scripts > Script Events Manager.
2. Event = Open Document, Script = Browse... C:\scripts\log_open.jsx, Add.
3. Every document opened from now on runs the logging script.
tools.notes: A faulty event script can make Photoshop appear broken on every open - untick "Enable Events" to recover.

tools.name: Contact Sheet II
tools.description: Builds a multi-page contact sheet from a folder or a Bridge selection, laying out thumbnails on a grid with optional filename captions. Used for client proof sheets, asset indexes and print catalogues.
tools.usage: File > Automate > Contact Sheet II...

parameters.name: Source Images
parameters.description: Folder (with subfolders), Bridge selection or open documents.

parameters.name: Document
parameters.description: Width, height, resolution, colour mode, bit depth and Flatten All Layers.

parameters.name: Thumbnails
parameters.description: Place across first or down first, columns and rows, Use Auto-Spacing, Rotate For Best Fit.

parameters.name: Use Filename As Caption
parameters.description: Font and size for the caption under each thumbnail.

tools.example: File > Automate > Contact Sheet II: Source = folder C:\shoot, Document 297 x 210 mm at 300 ppi, 5 columns x 4 rows, tick Use Filename As Caption at 9 pt.

tools.name: Fit Image
tools.description: Resamples the open document so it fits inside a width and height box without changing its aspect ratio, with an option not to enlarge small files. The building block of a resize action, because unlike Image Size it handles portrait and landscape files with one setting.
tools.usage: File > Automate > Fit Image...

parameters.name: Width / Height
parameters.description: The bounding box in pixels; the longest edge is fitted to it.

parameters.name: Don't Enlarge
parameters.description: Leaves images already smaller than the box untouched.

tools.example: Record an action: File > Automate > Fit Image, Width 2000, Height 2000, tick Don't Enlarge; then Save As JPEG. Run it from Batch over a mixed-orientation folder.

tools.name: Conditional Mode Change
tools.description: Changes the document's colour mode only if it currently matches one of the selected source modes, which stops an action failing when it meets a file that is already in the target mode. Designed specifically to be recorded inside actions.
tools.usage: File > Automate > Conditional Mode Change...

parameters.name: Source Mode
parameters.description: Tick any of Bitmap, Grayscale, Duotone, Indexed Color, RGB, CMYK, Lab, Multichannel (or click All).

parameters.name: Target Mode
parameters.description: The mode to convert to when the source matches.

tools.example: While recording: File > Automate > Conditional Mode Change, Source = All, Target = RGB Color. The action now safely handles CMYK, greyscale and indexed files.

tools.name: Crop and Straighten Photos
tools.description: Detects the individual photographs on a flatbed scan of several prints, then crops, straightens and opens each as its own document. The fastest way to digitise a box of prints; scanning against a contrasting background improves detection.
tools.usage: File > Automate > Crop and Straighten Photos (no dialog; it acts on the active document).
tools.example:
1. Scan four prints on the platen with a small gap between them.
2. File > Automate > Crop and Straighten Photos.
3. Four new straightened documents open, ready to save.
tools.notes: If it splits one photo into pieces, make a rough rectangular selection around a single photo first and run the command again.

tools.name: Load Files into Stack
tools.description: Opens a set of files as layers in one new document, with optional automatic alignment and conversion of the result into a Smart Object. The entry point for focus stacking, noise reduction by averaging, long-exposure simulation and crowd removal.
tools.usage: File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack...

parameters.name: Use
parameters.description: Files or Folder (or Add Open Files).

parameters.name: Attempt to Automatically Align Source Images
parameters.description: Runs Auto-Align Layers on the loaded layers.

parameters.name: Create Smart Object after Loading Layers
parameters.description: Required before the Stack Mode commands can be used.

tools.example:
1. File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack, choose 20 hand-held frames, tick both checkboxes.
2. Layer > Smart Objects > Stack Mode > Mean to average out the noise.

tools.name: Stack Modes (Layer > Smart Objects > Stack Mode)
tools.description: Statistical renderers applied across the layers inside a Smart Object: Mean and Median average away noise and moving objects, Maximum and Minimum keep the brightest or darkest pixel (star trails, light painting), Range, Standard Deviation, Variance, Summation, Entropy, Kurtosis and Skewness support scientific and forensic analysis.
tools.usage: Layer > Smart Objects > Stack Mode > <mode>, on a Smart Object created from a layer stack.

parameters.name: Mean
parameters.description: Average of all layers - noise reduction and simulated long exposure.

parameters.name: Median
parameters.description: Middle value - removes tourists and passing cars from a locked-off shot.

parameters.name: Maximum / Minimum
parameters.description: Brightest / darkest pixel across the stack - star trails, light trails.

parameters.name: Standard Deviation / Range
parameters.description: Highlights how much each pixel changed across the stack.

tools.example:
1. Shoot 10 frames of a busy square on a tripod.
2. File > Scripts > Load Files into Stack with "Create Smart Object" ticked.
3. Layer > Smart Objects > Stack Mode > Median - the people disappear.

tools.name: Export Layers to Files
tools.description: Writes every layer (or every visible layer) of the document to its own file in a chosen format, with a filename prefix and optional trimming to the layer's bounds. Used to hand off UI assets, sprite frames and per-layer renders.
tools.usage: File > Export > Layers to Files...

parameters.name: Destination / File Name Prefix
parameters.description: Output folder and the string prepended to each layer name.

parameters.name: Visible Layers Only
parameters.description: Skips hidden layers.

parameters.name: File Type
parameters.description: PSD, BMP, JPEG, PDF, Targa, TIFF, PNG-8, PNG-24, with per-format quality options.

parameters.name: Include ICC Profile
parameters.description: Embeds the document profile in each exported file.

tools.example: File > Export > Layers to Files: Destination C:\assets, Prefix "icon_", tick Visible Layers Only, File Type = PNG-24, Transparency on.
tools.notes: For modern asset export prefer File > Export > Export As or Generate > Image Assets (layer names ending in .png/.jpg auto-export on save).

tools.name: File > Scripts menu and script installation
tools.description: Runs a script on demand. File > Scripts > Browse... executes any .jsx or .psjs file from disk; scripts copied into the application's Presets/Scripts folder appear as named entries in the menu after a restart, where they can also be given a keyboard shortcut through Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts.
tools.usage: File > Scripts > Browse... (Ctrl+click for the last-used script), or File > Scripts > <name> for installed scripts. Install path on Windows: C:\Program Files\Adobe\Adobe Photoshop 2025\Presets\Scripts\.
tools.example:
1. Save export_all.jsx into Presets\Scripts.
2. Restart Photoshop - it appears as File > Scripts > export_all.
3. Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts > Application Menus > File > Scripts > export_all, assign Shift+F6.
tools.notes: Scripts placed in Presets/Scripts/Startup Scripts run every time Photoshop launches.

tools.name: app (Application object)
tools.description: The root of the ExtendScript DOM. It exposes the open documents, the active document, the foreground and background colours, preferences, the fonts list, the path to the application, and the scripting entry points doAction, load, open, purge, refresh, beep, notify and system. Setting app.displayDialogs and app.preferences.rulerUnits at the top of every script is standard practice.
tools.usage: app.<property|method>(...)  - e.g. app.documents, app.activeDocument, app.foregroundColor, app.displayDialogs, app.preferences.rulerUnits, app.doAction(), app.open(), app.purge(), app.system()

parameters.name: app.displayDialogs
parameters.description: DialogModes.NO suppresses every dialog - essential for unattended runs.

parameters.name: app.preferences.rulerUnits
parameters.description: Units.PIXELS, Units.INCHES, Units.CM ... - decides how bare numbers are interpreted.

parameters.name: app.foregroundColor / backgroundColor
parameters.description: SolidColor objects used by fill and paint operations.

parameters.name: app.path
parameters.description: Folder object pointing at the Photoshop installation.

tools.name: app.documents and Documents.add()
tools.description: The collection of open documents, indexable by position or by name, plus the factory that creates a new one. Documents.add takes width, height, resolution, name, mode, initial fill, pixel aspect ratio, bit depth and colour profile.
tools.usage:
app.documents.length
app.documents[0]
app.documents.getByName("shot.psd")
app.documents.add(width, height, resolution, name, mode, initialFill, pixelAspectRatio, bitsPerChannel, colorProfileName)

tools.name: app.open() and Document.close()
tools.description: Opens a file from a File object, optionally with a format-specific open-options object (for example CameraRAWOpenOptions, PDFOpenOptions or EPSOpenOptions), and closes a document with or without saving. Always close with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES in a batch loop or Photoshop will block on a dialog.
tools.usage:
app.open(file [, openAs] [, asSmartObject])
doc.close(SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES | SAVECHANGES | PROMPTTOSAVECHANGES)

tools.name: Document (object)
tools.description: One open file. Carries width, height, resolution, mode, bitsPerChannel, name, fullName, path, colorProfileName, activeLayer, activeChannels, layers, artLayers, layerSets, channels, pathItems, selection, historyStates, layerComps, info (metadata) and the methods that transform, save, export, print and close it.
tools.usage:
var doc = app.activeDocument;
doc.width / doc.height / doc.resolution / doc.mode / doc.bitsPerChannel
doc.activeLayer / doc.layers / doc.artLayers / doc.layerSets / doc.selection
doc.saveAs() / doc.exportDocument() / doc.close() / doc.duplicate() / doc.print()

tools.name: ArtLayer
tools.description: A single pixel, type, shape or adjustment layer. Properties include name, visible, opacity, fillOpacity, blendMode, kind, bounds, allLocked, grouped (clipped) and textItem; methods include translate, resize, rotate, move, duplicate, merge, rasterize, link, remove, invert, desaturate, applyStyle and the filter/adjustment helpers.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: LayerKind.NORMAL, TEXT, SOLIDFILL, GRADIENTFILL, PATTERNFILL, LEVELS, CURVES, SMARTOBJECT, ... - set it to TEXT to turn a new layer into type.

parameters.name: blendMode
parameters.description: BlendMode.NORMAL, MULTIPLY, SCREEN, OVERLAY, SOFTLIGHT, LUMINOSITY, ...

parameters.name: bounds
parameters.description: Array of four UnitValues [left, top, right, bottom] - the layer's pixel extent.

tools.name: LayerSet (layer group)
tools.description: A layer group. Holds its own artLayers and nested layerSets collections plus name, visible, opacity, blendMode, bounds and the same move/duplicate/merge/remove methods as a layer. Iterate layerSets recursively to walk an entire layer tree.
tools.usage:
var g = doc.layerSets.add();
g.name / g.artLayers / g.layerSets / g.visible / g.opacity / g.merge() / g.remove()

tools.name: Document.selection (Selection object)
tools.description: The active pixel selection. Methods: select (from a polygon of points), selectAll, deselect, invert, feather, expand, contract, smooth, grow, similar, translate, rotate, resize, fill, stroke, clear, copy, cut, store (to a channel) and load (from a channel).
tools.usage:
doc.selection.select(region [, type] [, feather] [, antiAlias])
doc.selection.selectAll() / deselect() / invert() / feather(px) / expand(px) / contract(px)
doc.selection.fill(color [, mode] [, opacity] [, preserveTransparency])
doc.selection.store(channel) / doc.selection.load(channel)

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: SelectionType.REPLACE, EXTEND, DIMINISH, INTERSECT.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Array of [x, y] point pairs describing a closed polygon in current ruler units.

parameters.name: bounds
parameters.description: doc.selection.bounds returns [left, top, right, bottom]; reading it throws if nothing is selected.

tools.name: Document.channels (Channel object)
tools.description: The component, spot and alpha channels of a document. Alpha channels are how selections are stored and restored in a script; each channel exposes name, kind, visible, opacity, colour, its histogram, and duplicate/remove methods.
tools.usage:
doc.channels.length / doc.channels.getByName("Alpha 1") / doc.channels.add()
doc.activeChannels = [doc.channels[0]]
channel.kind = ChannelType.MASKEDAREA | SELECTEDAREA | SPOTCOLOR
channel.histogram

tools.name: Document.pathItems (PathItem object)
tools.description: Vector paths in the document. PathItems are created from arrays of SubPathInfo/PathPointInfo objects, or from an existing selection with makeWorkPath, and can be converted back with makeSelection, painted with strokePath, filled with fillPath or turned into a vector mask.
tools.usage:
doc.pathItems.add(name, subPathInfoArray)
pathItem.makeSelection([feather] [, antiAlias] [, operation])
pathItem.strokePath(ToolType.BRUSH) / pathItem.fillPath(color)
doc.selection.makeWorkPath(tolerance)

tools.name: TextItem
tools.description: The type properties of a text layer: contents, font (PostScript name), size, color, justification, kind (POINTTEXT or PARAGRAPHTEXT), position, leading, tracking, baselineShift, capitalization, antiAliasMethod, width/height for paragraph text, plus warp settings and convertToShape/createPath.
tools.notes: font takes the PostScript name ("ArialMT", "Helvetica-Bold"), not the display name. Enumerate app.fonts to find it.

tools.name: SolidColor and colour objects
tools.description: Colour values for fills, strokes, type and swatches. A SolidColor wraps rgb, cmyk, lab, hsb and gray sub-objects; set whichever model suits and Photoshop converts. Related classes are the save/export option objects and UnitValue for measurements.

tools.name: Document.resizeImage(), resizeCanvas(), rotateCanvas(), trim(), crop()
tools.description: The geometry methods of a document. resizeImage resamples the pixels (pass null for a dimension to keep the aspect ratio), resizeCanvas changes the canvas around the existing pixels from an anchor, rotateCanvas turns the whole document by an angle, trim removes uniform borders and crop cuts to a rectangle with optional rotation and resampling.
tools.usage:
doc.resizeImage(width, height, resolution, resampleMethod)
doc.resizeCanvas(width, height, anchor)
doc.rotateCanvas(angle)
doc.trim(TrimType.TRANSPARENT | TOPLEFT | BOTTOMRIGHT, top, left, bottom, right)
doc.crop(bounds [, angle] [, width] [, height] [, resolution])

parameters.name: resampleMethod
parameters.description: ResampleMethod.BICUBIC, BICUBICSHARPER (reduction), BICUBICSMOOTHER (enlargement), NEARESTNEIGHBOR, BILINEAR, PRESERVEDETAILS, NONE.

parameters.name: anchor
parameters.description: AnchorPosition.MIDDLECENTER, TOPLEFT, BOTTOMRIGHT and the other six positions.

tools.name: ArtLayer filter methods (applyGaussianBlur, applyUnSharpMask, ...)
tools.description: Direct DOM wrappers for the most-used filters, avoiding Action Manager descriptors. The family includes applyGaussianBlur, applyMotionBlur, applyRadialBlur, applySmartBlur, applyLensBlur, applyUnSharpMask, applySharpen, applySharpenEdges, applyAddNoise, applyDespeckle, applyDustAndScratches, applyMedianNoise, applyHighPass, applyMaximum, applyMinimum, applyOffset, applyPinch, applyPolarCoordinates, applyRipple, applyShear, applySpherize, applyTwirl, applyWave, applyZigZag, applyDisplace, applyLensFlare, applyTextureFill and applyCustomFilter.
tools.usage:
layer.applyGaussianBlur(radius)
layer.applyUnSharpMask(amount, radius, threshold)
layer.applyMotionBlur(angle, radius)
layer.applyHighPass(radius)
layer.applyAddNoise(amount, NoiseDistribution.GAUSSIAN, monochromatic)
tools.notes: These methods fail on smart objects, type layers and adjustment layers - rasterize or target a pixel layer first. Filters with no DOM wrapper (Camera Raw, Liquify, Blur Gallery) need executeAction or batchPlay.

tools.name: ArtLayer adjustment methods (adjustLevels, adjustCurves, ...)
tools.description: DOM wrappers for destructive image adjustments applied to a pixel layer: adjustLevels, adjustCurves, adjustBrightnessContrast, autoLevels, autoContrast, desaturate, invert, equalize, posterize, threshold, mixChannels, photoFilter, selectiveColor, colorBalance, applyStyle and merge/rasterize helpers.
tools.usage:
layer.adjustLevels(inputBlack, inputWhite, gamma, outputBlack, outputWhite)
layer.adjustCurves(curveShapeArray)
layer.adjustBrightnessContrast(brightness, contrast)
layer.autoLevels() / autoContrast() / desaturate() / invert() / equalize()
layer.posterize(levels) / layer.threshold(level)
tools.notes: These write pixels. For non-destructive work create an adjustment layer with executeAction/batchPlay instead.

tools.name: Document.saveAs() and save-option objects
tools.description: Writes the document to disk in a chosen format, driven by a format-specific options object: PhotoshopSaveOptions, JPEGSaveOptions, PNGSaveOptions, TiffSaveOptions, GIFSaveOptions, BMPSaveOptions, EPSSaveOptions, PDFSaveOptions, TargaSaveOptions and others. `asCopy` writes a copy and leaves the open document pointing at the original file.
tools.usage:
doc.saveAs(file, options [, asCopy] [, extensionType])
doc.save()   // saves over the existing file

parameters.name: JPEGSaveOptions
parameters.description: quality (0-12), embedColorProfile, formatOptions (STANDARDBASELINE/OPTIMIZEDBASELINE/PROGRESSIVE), matte, scans.

parameters.name: PNGSaveOptions
parameters.description: interlaced, compression (0-9).

parameters.name: PhotoshopSaveOptions
parameters.description: layers, alphaChannels, annotations, spotColors, embedColorProfile.

parameters.name: TiffSaveOptions
parameters.description: imageCompression (NONE/LZW/ZIP/JPEG), layers, byteOrder, transparency.

parameters.name: extensionType
parameters.description: Extension.LOWERCASE or Extension.UPPERCASE.

tools.name: Document.exportDocument() and ExportOptionsSaveForWeb
tools.description: Exports through the Save for Web engine (or as Illustrator paths), which is how a script produces small, web-ready PNG and JPEG files with a controlled palette, transparency and optional metadata stripping.
tools.usage: doc.exportDocument(file, ExportType.SAVEFORWEB | ILLUSTRATORPATHS, exportOptions)

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: SaveDocumentType.JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP.

parameters.name: PNG8
parameters.description: false for PNG-24 (true colour with alpha), true for an 8-bit palette.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: 0-100 for JPEG.

parameters.name: transparency / matte
parameters.description: Keep alpha, or composite onto a matte colour.

parameters.name: interlaced / optimized / includeProfile
parameters.description: Standard Save for Web switches.

tools.name: app.doAction()
tools.description: Plays a recorded Action by name from a named Action Set, letting a script hand off work that is easier to record than to code (Liquify presets, Blur Gallery, Camera Raw settings, complex layer styles). The action must already be loaded in the Actions panel; app.load(file) loads an .atn first.
tools.usage:
app.doAction(actionName, actionSetName)
app.load(new File("C:/actions/house.atn"))
tools.notes: Action names are case-sensitive and locale-dependent; an action recorded in a different language build may not be found by name.

tools.name: executeAction() and executeActionGet()
tools.description: The Action Manager. executeAction plays an internal command described by an ActionDescriptor (with ActionReference targets and ActionList values) and reaches every feature the DOM omits - adjustment layers, layer styles, Content-Aware Fill, Blur Gallery, Select Subject, Generative Fill and so on. executeActionGet reads properties back from the application, document, layer or channel.

parameters.name: put/get methods
parameters.description: putInteger, putDouble, putString, putBoolean, putEnumerated, putUnitDouble, putReference, putObject, putList - with matching getters on the result descriptor.

parameters.name: ActionReference
parameters.description: putEnumerated(classID, formID, typeID), putName, putIndex, putIdentifier, putProperty - addresses what the command acts on.

parameters.name: displayDialogs
parameters.description: DialogModes.NO, ALL or ERROR.

tools.notes: Record the descriptors for any UI command with the free ScriptingListener plugin, which logs them to ScriptingListenerJS.log on the desktop.

tools.name: stringIDToTypeID() and charIDToTypeID()
tools.description: Convert a command, class or key name into the integer type ID that ActionDescriptor and ActionReference require. stringIDToTypeID takes a readable identifier ("gaussianBlur", "layerID"); charIDToTypeID takes a legacy four-character code ("GsnB", "Lyr " - note the significant trailing space). typeIDToStringID and typeIDToCharID reverse them.
tools.notes: Prefer stringIDToTypeID in new code: the four-character codes are cryptic and a missing trailing space is a classic silent bug.

tools.name: ScriptUI dialogs, $.writeln and File/Folder objects
tools.description: The ExtendScript environment around the Photoshop DOM. ScriptUI builds dialogs and palettes (Window, Group, Panel, StaticText, EditText, Button, DropDownList, Checkbox, ListBox, ProgressBar) either by construction or from a resource string. $.writeln logs to the ExtendScript console, $.sleep, $.getenv and $.os expose the host, and the File/Folder classes handle disk I/O, selection dialogs and path conversion.
tools.notes: File paths in ExtendScript use forward slashes or URI encoding; File.fsName gives the platform-native path.

tools.name: UXP: require('photoshop').app
tools.description: The modern Photoshop scripting DOM, available to UXP plugins and to .psjs script files (Photoshop 23.3+). It is promise-based and largely mirrors the ExtendScript object model - app.documents, app.activeDocument, doc.layers, layer.name, doc.createLayer, doc.saveAs, doc.resizeImage, doc.crop - but runs on a modern JavaScript engine with ES6+, async/await and npm-style modules.
tools.notes: UXP plugins are built and side-loaded with the UXP Developer Tool and distributed through Adobe Exchange / Creative Cloud Desktop as .ccx packages.

tools.name: UXP: action.batchPlay()
tools.description: The UXP equivalent of executeAction: it plays an array of actionJSON descriptors through the Photoshop event queue and returns their results as a promise. Because actionJSON is plain JSON rather than constructed ActionDescriptor objects, it is far easier to read, generate and template than the ExtendScript Action Manager, and it reaches every command in the application.
tools.usage:
const { batchPlay } = require("photoshop").action;
const result = await batchPlay(descriptors, options);

parameters.name: descriptors
parameters.description: Array of objects with _obj (the command), _target (an array of references) and the command's keys.

parameters.name: options.synchronousExecution
parameters.description: true runs inline and returns results directly; default is asynchronous.

parameters.name: options.modalBehavior
parameters.description: "execute", "wait" or "fail" - how to behave if a modal dialog is open.

parameters.name: dialogOptions
parameters.description: Per-descriptor: "dontDisplay", "display" or "silent".

tools.notes: The Alchemist plugin (Adobe Exchange) records actionJSON for any UI action, the UXP counterpart of ScriptingListener.

tools.name: UXP: core.executeAsModal() and the imaging API
tools.description: executeAsModal wraps any code that changes the document in a modal scope so Photoshop can suspend the UI and history correctly; without it, document mutations from a UXP plugin are rejected. Its executionContext also offers hostControl for suspend/resume history and a reportProgress callback. The separate imaging module (require('photoshop').imaging) reads and writes raw pixel data - getPixels, putPixels, encodeImageData, getLayerMask - for filters and analysis written in JavaScript.
tools.notes: Always call imageData.dispose() - undisposed buffers leak memory quickly on large documents.

tools.name: COM: Photoshop.Application
tools.description: The Windows COM automation server. Creating the `Photoshop.Application` ProgID starts or attaches to Photoshop and exposes Application members (Visible, Documents, ActiveDocument, Preferences, DisplayDialogs, Open, Load, Quit, Purge, Refresh) plus the scripting bridges DoJavaScript, DoJavaScriptFile and DoAction. This is how Python, C#, VBScript, PowerShell, Excel VBA or a web server drives Photoshop without writing a launcher script.

parameters.name: Open(path)
parameters.description: Opens a document and makes it active.

parameters.name: DoJavaScript(code, args, execMode)
parameters.description: Evaluates ExtendScript and returns the value of the last expression as a string.

parameters.name: DoJavaScriptFile(path, args, execMode)
parameters.description: Runs a .jsx file, optionally passing an argument array.

parameters.name: DoAction(action, from)
parameters.description: Plays a recorded action from a named set.

parameters.name: ActiveDocument
parameters.description: The Document object, with Close(saveOptions), ResizeImage, SaveAs, Flatten, Layers and so on.

tools.example:
import win32com.client as win32
ps = win32.Dispatch("Photoshop.Application")
ps.Visible = True
ps.Open(r"C:\in\shot.psd")
layers = ps.DoJavaScript("app.activeDocument.layers.length")
ps.DoAction("Export 1200", "Web")
ps.ActiveDocument.Close(2)  # psDoNotSaveChanges
print("layers:", layers)
tools.notes: COM is Windows-only and requires Photoshop to be installed and licensed on the machine, running in an interactive desktop session. Version-suffixed ProgIDs (Photoshop.Application.180) pin a specific release.

tools.name: Photoshop API (cloud REST)
tools.description: Adobe's hosted PSD service, part of Firefly Services. It edits PSDs server-side with no Photoshop installation: /documentOperations edits layers (text, smart object replacement, visibility, add/edit/delete, layer effects), /renditionCreate renders PSDs to JPEG/PNG/TIFF/PSD at requested sizes, /documentCreate builds a new PSD, /smartObject swaps smart object contents, /text edits text layers, and /actionJSON plays recorded action steps expressed as JSON. v2 unifies these behind /v2/create-composite. Calls are asynchronous: the response carries a job URL to poll, and files move via presigned storage URLs.
tools.usage:
POST https://image.adobe.io/pie/psdService/documentOperations
POST https://image.adobe.io/pie/psdService/renditionCreate
POST https://image.adobe.io/pie/psdService/smartObject
POST https://image.adobe.io/pie/psdService/text
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <IMS token>, x-api-key: <client id>, Content-Type: application/json

parameters.name: inputs
parameters.description: Array of {href, storage} - the source PSD, as a presigned GET URL (external, azure, dropbox) or an Adobe-hosted asset.

parameters.name: options.layers
parameters.description: Layer edits: name/id targeting, text.content and character styles, smartObject.href, visible, locked, add/edit/delete/move operations.

parameters.name: outputs
parameters.description: Array of {href, storage, type, width, quality, overwrite} - where the rendition is written.

parameters.name: job polling
parameters.description: The 202 response returns _links.self; GET it until status is succeeded or failed.

tools.notes: Authentication is an Adobe IMS OAuth server-to-server token scoped to the Photoshop API in a Developer Console project. Not every desktop feature is available server-side; check the endpoint's supported operations before designing a pipeline.
